decisions.where: Roles, the `accountant` line: one on the accounting team who prints a client's invoice at that client's tax rate, with `invoicer`'s command; Concept, its first line: `invoicer` prints the finished invoice from the invoice lines as the `accountant`'s spreadsheet holds them.
Roles, the `installer` line: a developer who sets up `invoicer`'s command on each `accountant`'s machine, installing Python and `invoicer` in place of the `accountant`.

The whole vision: `invoicer` for the product, `invoicer`'s command for what is run, `accountant` for one who prints, and the `accountant`'s machine for where it runs, each written the same way throughout.
Objectives and key results, the `O1` item.
Objectives and key results, the `O2` item.
Objectives and key results: the tasks the key results measure, from opening the spreadsheet to the printed invoice (`KR1.2`) and from starting a setup to `invoicer`'s command running (`KR2.2`).

Objectives and key results: `KR1.1`, `KR1.2`, `KR2.1`, `KR2.2`, each with Lower is better; `KR1.2` and `KR2.2` ranked after `KR1.1` and `KR2.1` in their own lines; the template's ranking and no-targets paragraph, whose reason is that a measure made a target stops being a good measure.

Objectives and key results: O1 is the `accountant`'s and O2 the `installer`'s, so the command and the README's part for the `accountant` serve O1 and the README's setup section serves O2; the vision lists no README pieces, which the README's own points settle.
Concept, its first line: `invoicer` prints the finished invoice from the invoice lines as the `accountant`'s spreadsheet holds them, plus the client's tax rate.
Concept, the three ideas: The spreadsheet as it is, Nothing wrong prints, and The rate given each time.

Concept, the line under each idea: neither the `accountant` nor the `installer` has a format to learn or set up; where `invoicer` can't read a line or the rate, it prints only a message naming what to fix; each time the `accountant` prints an invoice they give the rate, so the `installer` sets up no rates.

more.where: Roles, the `accountant` line: the `accountant` prints with `invoicer`'s command, so the reader knows the command before `KR2.1`.
Objectives and key results: `KR1.2` and `KR2.2` each say Lower is better, ranked after `KR1.1` or `KR2.1`, beside the template's line that `KR1.1` and `KR2.1` come first.

Concept: each idea in one sentence, the unreadable line and the rate made the subject's own action; the Concept's first line in one sentence of 20 words. The template's fixed ranking and no-targets paragraph stays word for word, so its plural with comes and its colon remain.

Concept: `invoicer` prints the finished invoice and prints no invoice, in place of returns and the print; the no-targets line gives the plain reason, a measure made a target stops being a good measure, before it names Goodhart's law. The O and KR labels get no line of their own, as the template takes none.

The whole vision: `invoicer` in code format each time, `invoicer`'s command in place of the command, each `accountant`'s machine in place of the accounting team's machines, and `accountant` and `installer` in code format each time.

settled.point: the template's fixed words against the kept Mores
settled.decided: The vision holds the template's blocks and no others, and its ranking and no-targets paragraph word for word: `KR1.1` and `KR2.1` comes first, and Goodhart's law with its reason. The Mores land in the slots: the ranking of `KR1.2` and `KR2.2` in their own lines, and the command in the `accountant` line.
settled.ground: rn's check holds the deliverable to the product-vision template, and refuses any line beside it, so an opening job line, a first line under Roles, and lines defining O and KR can't stand. The N5 More's plural with comes and the N6 More's O and KR labels come from the template's own words, which this round can't change.

settled.decided: `invoicer` prints the finished invoice from the invoice lines as the `accountant`'s spreadsheet holds them, plus the client's tax rate.
settled.ground: The template asks the one way as one sentence that goes on from the product's name, and the check takes at most 20 words. It keeps Cut decision 5/0's meaning: the lines as the accountant keeps them and the rate go in, the finished invoice prints.

settled.ground: The template takes one short sentence for what each idea gives, and at most three ideas, so the accountant's and the installer's sides of an idea share a sentence.
